title: Putting up a fence or a shed in Sebastian? The height limits, the paperwork and the anchoring rules
seoTitle: Sebastian Fence & Shed Rules: Heights, Permits, Anchors
description: Sebastian homeowners: fence height limits front and back, the survey and easement affidavit, shed size limits, tie-down rules and where a shed can sit.
dek: Cooler weather is project weather. Before the posts go in or the shed kit shows up, here is what the City of Sebastian asks for, in plain English.
facebook: Thinking about a new fence or a shed this fall? In Sebastian there's a 4-foot limit out front, a 6-foot limit out back, and real rules for tying a shed down. Here's what the city asks for before you start.

body.text: Fall is when a lot of Sebastian yards get their projects. The heat backs off, the rain slows down, and that fence you have been talking about for two years finally looks doable. Same with the shed for the mower and the hurricane supplies.

Both need a permit from the City of Sebastian Building Department if your home is inside city limits. The city's permit sheets for fences and sheds are short, but they have a few details that trip people up. Here they are.

body.title: The short version
body.text: Fences can be up to 6 feet tall in the rear setback and 4 feet in the front setback. You need a survey showing where the fence goes, and a recorded affidavit if it crosses an easement. Shed kits top out at 10 by 10 feet and must be strapped down with cables and auger anchors. A shed in the backyard has to stay at least 10 feet from the rear property line and out of any dedicated easement.
Fences: how tall, and what the city wants to see

The city's fence permit sheet sets two height limits. In the rear setback, a fence can be up to 6 feet. In the front setback, the limit is 4 feet. The height is measured from the inside of the fence line.

Watch out on corner lots. Sebastian's land development code says that on corner lots and through lots, every yard that faces a street counts as a front yard for setback purposes. That can change where a 6-foot fence is allowed, so ask the Building Department before you order materials.
To apply, the sheet asks for:

items: One survey of your property with the fence location clearly marked.
The type of fence: wood, chain link, aluminum, vinyl, wrought iron or concrete.
If any part of the fence sits in an easement, a utility easement affidavit, notarized by the owner and the contractor, and recorded at the Indian River County Courthouse recording office.
If your home is in a subdivision, a subdivision work authorization affidavit with the owner's notarized signature.

body.text: One more: if the fence goes around a pool, it has to meet the pool barrier rules in the Florida Building Code. The city's sheet points to that section directly. A pool fence is a safety barrier, not just a property line.

body.title: Why the easement affidavit matters
body.text: Building a fence in an easement is not banned in Sebastian, but it takes a notarized affidavit signed by both the owner and the contractor, recorded with the county. Check your survey for easement lines before you pick a fence route, so the paperwork does not surprise you.
Sheds: size limits and who can build them
The city's shed permit sheet splits sheds into two kinds: kits you buy pre-made, and sheds built on site.

items: Shed kits: maximum size 10 by 10 feet. You need the manufacturer's plans with tie-down details and the manufacturer's current approval letter from the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation.
Site-built by a licensed contractor: up to 400 square feet, with plan details for the floor, roof and walls, including how it is anchored.
Site-built by the owner: up to 120 square feet, with the same plan details.
Anything bigger: plans prepared and sealed by a licensed design professional.

body.text: You also need a survey showing where the shed will go. If your home is on septic and you plan a concrete slab, the sheet says the survey must be stamped by the Indian River County Health Department. That protects your tank and drainfield from ending up under concrete.
Tying it down: the anchoring rule

This is the part that matters most in hurricane country. For shed kits, the city requires at least two 3/16-inch stranded cables over the top of the shed, one in front and one in back. Each cable must be tightly secured to the eye of an auger anchor on each side, with at least two cable clamps at every connection.
The auger anchors must be at least 1/2 inch in diameter and go at least 2 feet into the ground. Site-built sheds need plan details showing they meet the required wind loads.
Where a shed can sit in your yard

Sebastian's land development code lets a detached shed sit in the required rear yard of a single-family lot, with limits. It must stay at least 10 feet from the rear property line, it cannot be inside a dedicated easement, and the code caps these structures at 400 square feet and 12 feet tall. For side setbacks on your lot, ask the Building Department.
What to do before you start

items: Confirm you are inside Sebastian city limits. If not, Indian River County handles your permit.
Pull out your survey and find the property lines and any easements. If you cannot find it, check your closing papers.
If you have an HOA, get its approval in writing. HOA rules can be stricter than the city's.

For a fence: mark the route on the survey, note the fence type, and keep it to 4 feet in the front setback and 6 feet in the rear. If you have a corner lot, ask the Building Department which yards count as front yards.
For a shed: pick a kit 10 by 10 or smaller, or plan for a contractor-built or sealed design. Keep it 10 feet off the rear line and out of the easement.
If you are on septic and pouring a slab, get the survey stamped by the county health department first.
If you hire someone, check the license at myfloridalicense.com and have them pull the permit.

body.text: A fence or shed is a small project, but a permit and a proper tie-down make it one you will not have to redo. A few minutes with your survey now beats moving a fence later.

faq.q: How tall can a fence be in Sebastian, FL?
faq.a: The City of Sebastian's fence permit sheet allows up to 6 feet in the rear setback and up to 4 feet in the front setback, measured from the inside of the fence line. On corner lots, every yard that faces a street counts as a front yard for setbacks.

faq.q: Do I need a permit for a fence in Sebastian?
faq.a: Yes. The City of Sebastian Building Department issues fence permits. You need a survey showing the fence location and type, plus a recorded utility easement affidavit if the fence sits in an easement.

faq.q: Do I need a permit for a shed in Sebastian?
faq.a: Yes. The city asks for a survey showing the location and either the manufacturer's plans with tie-down details and state approval letter for a kit, or plan details for a site-built shed. Kits are limited to 10 by 10 feet.

faq.q: How close to the property line can I put a shed in Sebastian?
faq.a: Sebastian's land development code says a detached shed in the rear yard of a single-family lot must stay at least 10 feet from the rear property line and cannot sit in a dedicated easement. Ask the Building Department about side setbacks for your lot.

faq.q: How do you tie down a shed in Sebastian?
faq.a: For shed kits, the city requires at least two 3/16-inch stranded cables over the top, front and back, each secured to auger anchors on both sides with two cable clamps per connection. Anchors must be at least 1/2 inch in diameter and 2 feet deep.
